newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government to discuss copper deal Friday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government to discuss copper deal Friday.

text.p: Zaire's full cabinet will discuss a joint venture deal between state-run mining company Gecamines and a major foreign partner at its next meeting on Friday, the government spokesman said on Tuesday.
Bogou Makeli said ministers held a preparatory meeting on Tuesday on the proposals for mining a huge copper and cobalt deposits at Tenke Fungurume in the mineral-rich southern region of Shaba.
The full cabinet would meet on Friday to discuss the matter, he added.

Canadian mining and exploration company Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd has said that Geneva-based Swedish financier Adolf Lundin is negotiating the deal on its behalf and on Friday it said it was close to closing the deal.
A consortium led by a second Canadian company, Cornucopia Resources Ltd, which included metals giants Inco Ltd and Phelps Dodge, has said it is still in the running.

If approved, the project would be the first major joint venture between Gecamines and a foreign partner. It would also be the first significant investment in Zaire by a private mining company since the 1970s.
The deal covers development of deposits which could yield 100,000 tonnes a year of copper and 8,000 tonnes of cobalt.

Sources close to the deal say investment in phase one would be around $350 million. A feasibility study between one and two years could lead to the first production of copper after as little four and a half years.
Lundin is also chairman of Vancouver-based International Petroleum Corp. The deal has no link with International Petroleum Corp.
